findings.title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when no `embed_category` row exists
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the query returns a row. `site_settings` only stores rows for settings an admin changed. On a fresh install, or any site that never set `embed_category`, the result set is empty, `[0]` is `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration. The fallback on line 15 has the same problem: `execute(...)[0]['value']` for `uncategorized_category_id` also breaks if that row is not present yet. Check for an empty result before indexing and default to a safe category id.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL unescaped
findings.body: Old `embeddable_hosts` values could be `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`. The migration inserts each line with raw SQL, so the model's `before_validation` that strips the scheme and path never runs. Rows keep the `http://` prefix (and `\r` or whitespace if the setting had it), and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so they never match. Every existing site that used the scheme form silently loses embedding after upgrade. The value is also interpolated as `'#{h}'` with no quoting or escaping, so a host containing a single quote breaks the migration, or injects SQL. Strip scheme, path and whitespace in Ruby and use `quote`/sanitization.

findings.title: before_validation calls `sub!` on a possibly-nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil, for example `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?`, or a POST to the controller without `embeddable_host[host]`. The user gets a 500 instead of a validation error. The `sub!` calls also mutate the caller's string in place. Guard with `host.present?` or use non-destructive `sub`.

findings.title: Hosts with a port (or uppercase) can be saved but never match
findings.body: The validation regex explicitly allows `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the normalizer keeps the port. But `record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host`, which never includes the port, so a host like `example.com:8080` is accepted and then never matches any referer. The right-hand side is also not downcased, so a mixed-case referer or embed URL fails against the lowercased column. Either reject ports on save or compare against `host:port`, and downcase the lookup value.

findings.title: update/destroy dereference a nil record for unknown ids
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing or already-deleted id. `destroy` then calls `nil.destroy`, and `update` passes nil to `save_host`, which calls `nil.host=`. Both raise NoMethodError and return a 500. Double-clicking delete or a stale admin page hits this. Use `find` and let Discourse's RecordNotFound handling return a 404, or add an explicit not-found check. A missing `params[:embeddable_host]` has the same effect in `save_host`.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. All the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. It works only because Fabrication loads every file in the directory, but it looks like an accidental swap. Anyone searching for the category fabricator or the embeddable host one will look in the wrong file, and the diff of both files is misleading. Restore the category fabricators to `category_fabricator.rb` and put only the embeddable_host fabricator in its own file.

findings.title: New admin controllers have no behavioral tests
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert that the class inherits from `AdminController`. Nothing tests create/update/destroy of hosts, the uncategorized default, validation error rendering, non-staff access being denied, or the embedding show endpoint. The nil-record and nil-host crashes in this PR would have been caught by such tests. `embeddable_host_spec` also lacks cases for nil host, ports, case and duplicates.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests what it says
findings.body: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for any embeddable host. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false for an unsaved topic. It would still pass if host handling were broken. The behavior change (expandable posts no longer require a configured host) is untested, and the test name is misleading. Remove the case or rewrite it to reflect the actual condition.
